title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 339
text:
118. The existence of dependent children is a factor relevant to sentencing.318 Sentencing
guidelines say being a sole or primary carer for dependent relatives can be a mitigating
factor.319 It is therefore important that courts are informed of the defendant’s domestic
circumstances and determine sentence following the steps in R v Rosie Lee Petherick and
that the interference with the defendant's Article 8 rights is proportionate.

320 Indeed, where
the offender is on the cusp of custody and there would be an impact on dependants which
would make custody disproportionate, a community order should be imposed rather than a
custodial sentence.

119. Women are much more likely to be primary carers,321 with children far more directly affected
by a prison sentence as a result. A fifth of women prisoners are lone parents322 and around
17,200 children are separated from their mothers by imprisonment every year.323 Only 9% of
children whose mothers are in prison are cared for by their fathers in their mother’s absence,
and only 5% remain in their own home while she is imprisoned. By contrast, most children
with an imprisoned father remain with their mother.
